Summary
Data source overview: The post proposes Open Agency Architecture (OAA) – a modular, open-source framework intended to align advanced AI systems with democratically-chosen human objectives.  It motivates OAA by highlighting failure modes of current alignment methods (RLHF, scalable oversight, interpretability), sketches a “minimal-viable” human-in-the-loop prototype, and decomposes the work into nine concrete sub-projects (agenda setting, world modelling, preference elicitation and choice).  The document provides design sketches, early prototypes, and real-world test-beds such as participatory budgeting.

Inference strategy justification:  The paper is largely conceptual.  Where explicit empirical validation was missing I used moderate inference (edge-confidence = 2) to bridge gaps (e.g. mapping “two-player Nash prototype” onto an intervention deploying an automated Nash solver).  All interventions are limited to those the authors explicitly plan or that are an immediately implied next engineering step.

Extraction completeness explanation:  34 nodes (≈ 1 per 225 words) capture every distinct risk, problem analysis, theoretical insight, design principle, implementation mechanism, validation evidence, and proposed intervention mentioned.  All nine OAA sub-projects are represented and connected, resulting in one fully connected knowledge fabric from two top-level risks down to seven actionable interventions.

Key limitations
1. Validation evidence is still thin; confidence scores are therefore mostly 2–3.
2. Continuous-time-coalgebra work is extremely speculative; connecting it required inference with low confidence.
3. The road-map spans governance and software engineering: lifecycle & maturity classifications are approximate.

EXTRACTION CONFIDENCE[73]

How to improve the instruction set
• Allow an explicit “no empirical validation yet” flag so implementation nodes without evidence do not need weakly-supported edges.  
• Clarify how to map multi-year socio-technical programmes (like “build MVP prototype”) onto the 1-6 AI lifecycle when they include many phases.  
• Provide standard wording examples for “aliases” to reduce stylistic variance across 500 k extractions.
